content.title: Dilated cardiomyopathy or hypokinetic non-dilated cardiomyopathy: specific aspects of diagnosis and treatment
content.summary: Guidance on diagnostic criteria for DCM and HNDC, recommendations for genetic counselling and testing, and a minimal gene panel for familial DCM/HNDC.
diagnostic_criteria: DCM: LV dilatation and systolic dysfunction in the absence of known abnormal loading conditions or significant CAD.
HNDC: LV or biventricular global systolic dysfunction (LVEF <45%) without dilatation in the absence of known abnormal loading conditions or significant CAD.
DCM and HNDC can be considered familial if two or more first- or second-degree relatives have DCM or HNDC, or a first-degree relative has autopsy proven DCM and sudden death at <50 years of age.
genetic_counselling_and_testing: Indication: All patients with a diagnosis of DCM or HNDC and all first-degree adult relatives of these patients and a definite disease-causing mutation should be offered testing to identify genetically affected individuals at a preclinical phase.
First-degree adult relatives should have evaluation repeated every 5 years or less when aged <50 years or non-diagnostic abnormalities are found.
Clinical evaluation, ECG, echocardiography and possibly CMR must be performed in first-degree relatives of patients.
Results: Genetic testing can identify patients with DCM or HNDC at highest risk of arrhythmia and/or deserving other specific treatments.
content.minimal_gene_set_note: Minimal set of genes listed in the guideline as relevant for DCM/HNDC genetic testing.
